Author: CrownedPandaXIV
Name: XIV Fleet Companion
Description:
Got a massive fleet of submarines? Always struggling to see which ones need upgrades? Wanna see your multi-account fleet at a glance? Give this a try!

This plugin sends your fleet to the free XIV Fleet Companion app for Windows, which shows it all in one window. Get the app from https://github.com/CrownedPandaXIV/XIVFleetCompanion-Releases

Needs:
• AutoRetainer (from https://love.puni.sh/ment.json)

Works best with:
• Allagan Tools: bags, retainers' items and FC chests
• FC Tracker (from https://puni.sh/api/repository/erdelf): FC houses
• Submarine Tracker: voyage loot

Thanks to kawaii, NightmareXIV and the Puni.sh team (AutoRetainer), Critical_Impact (Allagan Tools), erdelf (FC Tracker) and Infi (Submarine Tracker) for their plugins.
Punchline: Here to help manage your EMPIAH!
Changelog:
Just this PC: your fleet can now live in one file on your PC instead of a PostgreSQL database, with nothing to install.

- A new setup is asked first where its fleet data should live:
- Just this PC: every game on this PC keeps the fleet in one file, %APPDATA%\XIV Fleet Companion\fleet.db. Syncing starts straight away. The XIV Fleet Companion app can't open the file, so you see your fleet in the game.
- Shared between PCs: a PostgreSQL database set up with the app (its Database Helper is enough), as before. A setup that already has a database connection is never asked and keeps using it.
- Several games at once. Games on the same PC share the file and can sync at the same moment; one waits for another to finish writing rather than fail. Tested with four separate processes writing at once.
- Not in a cloud or network folder. OneDrive, Dropbox, Google Drive and similar copy the file while a game writes to it, which can damage it, so the plugin refuses to keep it there and says why.
- It keeps itself up to date. The plugin adds what a newer version needs to the file (never removing anything) and replaces the fleet views when they change, all or nothing. A file a newer plugin in another game already updated is left alone, and the Status page says to update.
- Moving your fleet, either way (Settings → Move your fleet):
- from Just this PC to a shared database, when you get a second PC or want the app: set up an empty database with the app's Database Helper, enter its details, and move;
- from a shared database to Just this PC, when this is the only PC you play on (it warns you if another PC synced to the database in the last day).

Syncing waits while every table is copied, and other games on the PC wait to write. Then every row is compared on both sides, and only when all of it matches does anything switch. It never copies into a place that already has a fleet, and the side it came from is left as it was (a fleet file moved away is backed up before it's ever reused). If anything goes wrong, nothing changes.
- Every game on a PC goes the same way. The choice is kept beside the fleet file, so when one game chooses or moves, the others follow at their next sync. A second game on a PC that's already set up isn't asked.
- Daily backups. Once a day while a game runs, the file is copied into a Backups folder beside it, and the last 7 are kept. The Status page shows the newest and has Back up now.
- On Just this PC, Settings shows where the file is in place of the database login, and the Status page leaves out the database connection test and speed test. Text that pointed at the app says where to find it in the game instead, and the PCs page talks about the games on this PC.
- Without the app, the plugin does its part: it saves each sub's Next Rank date once an hour (as the app does while it's open), so Route Optimization's forecast line works on Just this PC too.
- The Supplies page's days can be changed in the game, on their own line under the table's buttons: how many days its use per day is measured over (3, 7, 14 or 30) and how many days of supplies to buy for (1 to 90), with the same checks as the app's Supplies tab.
- Everything the plugin writes and reads (syncing, every page, the edits made from the game, Trends) works on the file. The tests sync and edit the same made-up fleet into a PostgreSQL database and into a file, and every page must read the same from both.
- Gil & Market lists accounts by name.
